title: Car Pooling
description: Brute force to optimized: touching every location in a trip's range versus a difference array that marks only pickup and drop-off, checked with one sweep.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: A car has a given capacity, and only travels eastward. Given a list of trips, each [numPassengers, from, to], meaning numPassengers must be picked up at location from and dropped off at location to, return true if it is possible to pick up and drop off all passengers for every trip without the car ever exceeding capacity.

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["Each trip adds passengers across a RANGE of locations","A difference array, identical to Range Addition and Corporate Flight Bookings"],["Only whether capacity is ever exceeded matters, not the count at every single point necessarily","One prefix-sum sweep after marking all trips, checking the running total against capacity"]]}

blocks.text: This is Range Addition and Corporate Flight Bookings again: apply every trip's passenger count across its pickup-to-drop-off range, and check whether the running passenger count ever exceeds the car's capacity.

blocks.title: Analogy: Checking a Shuttle Never Overfills Between Stops
blocks.text: Picture a shuttle van picking up and dropping off passengers at various stops along a route, and needing to confirm the van never has more passengers aboard than its seats allow, at any point between stops.

blocks.caption: Mark +passengers at pickup, -passengers at drop-off; a running sum gives the current count

blocks.text: Between locations 3 and 5, both trips overlap, giving 2 + 3 = 5 passengers, exceeding the capacity of 4, so the answer is false.
The same overlap now totals exactly 5, which fits within the capacity of 5, so the answer is true.
Before applying every trip by touching each location in its range, notice this is exactly the difference array technique already used for Range Addition and Corporate Flight Bookings.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Each trip increases the passenger count by numPassengers starting at from, and decreases it back down starting at to (where that trip's passengers have already been dropped off).

Observation 2: Marking just those two points per trip, in a difference array, takes O(1) per trip instead of O(range length).

Observation 3: A single left-to-right running sum over the difference array reconstructs the exact passenger count at every location.

Observation 4: If that running count ever exceeds capacity at any point, the answer is false; otherwise, once every location has been checked, the answer is true.
This leads directly to marking each trip's two endpoints in a difference array, then sweeping once to check whether the running passenger count ever exceeds capacity.
For every trip, add its passenger count directly to every location from pickup to drop-off, then check if any location ever exceeds capacity.

items: Initialize a count array over every possible location.
For every trip, add numPassengers to every location from "from" to "to minus 1".
After all trips are applied, check whether any location's count exceeds capacity.

blocks.caption: Brute force flow: touch every location in a trip's range, for every trip

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Every location in a trip's range is updated directly and checked immediately.
This guarantees correctness, but revisits many locations across overlapping trips, redoing work unnecessarily.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(trips.length times average trip range length), up to O(n times 1000) in the worst case.
Space: O(1000) for the counts array.
Limitation: exactly like Range Addition, touching every location in a trip's range is unnecessary; only the two boundaries actually matter.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why touching every location is wasteful: a trip only changes the passenger count's "rate" at exactly two points, where it starts, and where it ends (passengers dropped off).

What can represent that instead: a difference array, where diff[from] += numPassengers marks the pickup, and diff[to] -= numPassengers marks the drop-off.

How is the true passenger count recovered: one left-to-right running sum over the difference array, exactly as in Range Addition.

The core idea: mark each trip's two boundaries in O(1), then sweep once, checking whether the running total ever exceeds capacity.

For every trip [numPassengers, from, to], add numPassengers to diff[from] and subtract numPassengers from diff[to]. Then sweep left to right, maintaining a running total; if it ever exceeds capacity, return false immediately, otherwise return true once the sweep completes.

blocks.caption: Optimized flow: mark trip endpoints in O(1), sweep once to check against capacity

blocks.text: Marking +numPassengers at from and -numPassengers at to means a running sum swept left to right includes those passengers at every location from "from" up to (but not including) "to", exactly matching when they are aboard. Since every trip's marks add together independently, checking the running total against capacity at every point during one single sweep correctly detects any overflow.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(trips.length plus max location), O(1) per trip to mark, plus one linear sweep.
Space: O(max location) for the difference array.

blocks.text: Car Pooling is Range Addition wearing yet another name: mark each trip's pickup and drop-off as a difference array update, then sweep once to check whether the running passenger count ever exceeds capacity.

items: Placing the drop-off mark at "to" instead of realizing passengers are no longer aboard exactly AT location "to" (the range is pickup-inclusive, drop-off-exclusive).
Checking capacity only at trip start/end points instead of during the full sweep, which could miss an overflow caused by overlapping trips elsewhere.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","Expected Behavior"],"rows":[["No trips at all","Always true, capacity is never exceeded."],["A single trip exactly at capacity","Still true, since capacity is not EXCEEDED, only met."]]}

blocks.text: Immediately recognizing this as a difference-array range-update problem, the same as Range Addition and Corporate Flight Bookings, is the fastest path to a correct and efficient solution.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "does this remind you of another problem", think: this is Range Addition, checking a running total against a capacity threshold instead of just returning the final array.

items: How would you find the exact location where capacity is first exceeded, not just whether it happens?
How would this change if trips could also be added or removed dynamically, one at a time, needing an answer after each change?
Range Addition and Corporate Flight Bookings, the same difference array technique.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The brute force runs in O(trips.length times range length) time; the optimized difference array approach runs in O(trips.length plus max location) time. Both use O(max location) space.

items: Pattern: the difference array technique, identical to Range Addition, checking a running total against a threshold.
Core Idea: mark each trip's pickup and drop-off in O(1), then sweep once, returning false the instant the running passenger count exceeds capacity.
Time: O(trips.length times range length) for the brute force, O(trips.length plus max location) for the optimized approach.
Most Important Observation: this is exactly Range Addition, just checking the running total against a capacity threshold instead of returning the final array.
Interview Difficulty: straightforward once recognized as a difference-array problem.
One line memory trick: mark pickup and drop-off, sweep once, watch for overflow.
